dial.summary: DXY at 101.93 and TIPS real yields at 2.89% remain structural headwinds, but the September NFP shock (+29K) has priced out near-term Fed hikes and the 2s10s curve steepened to +45bps — BTC.D holds firm at 58.5% with perpetual funding near neutral (0.0100% per 8h) confirming spot accumulation; stablecoin dominance edged down to ~10.1%, a constructive rotation signal; October 14 CPI is the single highest-impact catalyst for a macro regime shift.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.6T based on August 2026 data (latest available); US M2 $23.3T for August 2026 per Fed H.6; China M2 ~$53.2T, Eurozone ~$18.7T; September G4 M2 not yet available (6–8 week reporting lag); 4-week trend flat: no new confirmed September G4 data; YoY still meaningfully positive (not contracting); status neutral — confirmed rising 4-week trend required for supportive; ISM Prices at 77.9% and still-elevated CPI (~3.5% YoY) present a stagflation signal that complicates the liquidity expansion narrative; next G4 M2 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5%, released October 1 — ninth consecutive month of manufacturing expansion; 4-week trend flat: August 54.6% → September 54.5% = −0.1pp, within the flat threshold; New Orders Index 55.3% (bullish forward signal); Production Index 56.7%; Prices Index 77.9% (highest since mid-2021, a leading CPI upside signal); status neutral (above 50 but flat; supportive requires above 50 AND rising); next ISM Manufacturing release November 3, 2026.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at ~101.93 on October 2, 2026 (last trading session; October 4 is Sunday); post-NFP pullback from intraday highs above 102.20 after September payrolls missed badly (+29K vs 90K consensus); 4-week trend up: ~99.8 (Sep 3) → 101.93 (Oct 2) = +2.1% over 30 days, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY still above 100 threshold; a sustained close below 100 required to return to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next major DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.89% as of October 2, 2026; breakeven inflation rate 2.28% (stagflation premium building with ISM Prices at 77.9%); 4-week trend up: ~2.50% (Sep 3) → 2.89% (Oct 2) = +39bps over 30 days; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); 10Y nominal yield at 5.28% despite weak September NFP, reflecting fiscal and stagflation concerns; a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral; October 14 CPI is the next key real yield repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 2, 2026: 10Y Treasury 5.28%, 2Y Treasury 4.83% → 2s10s spread = +0.45% (+45bps); 4-week trend up (steepening): Sep 3 spread ~+42bps (10Y 4.762%, 2Y 4.342%) → Oct 2 +45bps = +3bps steepening over 30 days; status supportive (both positive AND steepening on 4-week basis); post-NFP curve steepening driven by 2Y falling faster than 10Y as Fed hold expectations rose sharply after +29K payroll miss; October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major yield curve catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,743,031M ($6.74T) for week ending September 30, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released October 1 (most recent; next H.4.1 release October 8 for week ending October 7); 4-week trend flat: Sep 2 $6,737,204M → Sep 30 $6,743,031M = +$5.8B marginal expansion within flat threshold on a $6.74T balance sheet; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration at Sep 15–16 FOMC where FFR was raised to 3.75%–4.00%); weak September NFP (+29K) raises probability of a Fed hold in October, supportive for balance sheet stability.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately 0.0100% per 8h as of October 2–3, 2026 per CoinGlass (latest available; October 4 is Sunday, direct feeds not accessible); rate remains well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; BTC price ~$85,900–86,500; BTC.D firm at 58.5%; 4-week trend up: rose from lower September levels (~0.001–0.007% range) to 0.0100% as BTC rallied; status supportive (significantly below 0.04% overheating threshold, confirming spot-driven price action rather than leveraged speculation); October 14 CPI and October 27–28 FOMC are next potential funding regime catalysts.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$291B as of early October 2026; total crypto market cap ~$2.89T (BTC.D 58.5%); stablecoin dominance ~10.1% (291/2890); 30-day trend down: ~10.4% (Sep 3) → ~10.1% (Oct 4) = −0.3pp over 30 days; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis, indicating capital rotation from stablecoin sidelines into crypto assets); USDT and USDC hold ~88.4% of stablecoin market share; declining dominance alongside stable total market cap reflects steady deployment into risk assets; October 14 CPI is the next major catalyst for stablecoin inflow/outflow dynamics.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — services sector is ~80% of US GDP; critical read given the September NFP shock (+29K vs 90K consensus): a strong services print above 55 would confirm late-cycle bifurcation (softening labor, resilient services) — the most challenging stagflation scenario for the Fed; August ISM Services was 54.2%; S&P Global Flash Services PMI surged to 58.7 in September (59-month high), a bullish leading signal; a print above 56 could revive October 27–28 FOMC hike speculation despite the NFP miss; ISM Manufacturing already at 54.5% with Prices at 77.9% — this release frames the full October FOMC setup.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (September 15–16, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — the meeting at which the Fed raised the fed funds rate 25bps to 3.75%–4.00%; minutes will reveal committee debate around further tightening pace, any dissents, and how members framed the balance between inflation (ISM Prices 77.9%, CPI ~3.5% YoY) and employment risks; critical to parse for October hold signals given the subsequent September NFP miss (+29K); market is pricing a high probability of a Fed hold at October 27–28 FOMC; minutes will clarify whether a pause was already being contemplated before the weak jobs data.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 4, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 4, 2026 — first claims reading fully capturing early-October labor conditions post the September NFP shock (+29K); prior weeks approximately 206K; closely watched for signs of labor market deterioration confirming the NFP miss is a trend rather than one-off; consecutive claims above 225K would reinforce Fed hold expectations for October 27–28; released the day after FOMC Minutes, providing a real-time follow-up to the September labor narrative.
